next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a long-running espionage group, tracked under many names, that exploits exposed servers and websites
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390, also called Emissary Panda or APT27, has been described since 2015 as a China-based espionage group. Reports show watering-hole attacks and exploits of unpatched servers, with HyperBro and PlugX among its tools.

sentences.t: Threat Group-3390 is also tracked as Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Dell SecureWorks researchers designated the group Threat Group 3390 and nicknamed it Emissary Panda. The article says the group is believed to be based in China.
Symantec's Threat Hunter Team tracks the group as Budworm, also known as LuckyMouse, Emissary Panda and APT27. Its report says the group is believed to have been active since at least 2013.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence says that since 2012 Linen Typhoon has focused on stealing intellectual property.
The German Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) describes APT27, also known as Emissary Panda, as a Chinese cyberespionage group.

Dell SecureWorks reported that most targets were in the automotive, electronic, aerospace, energy and pharmaceutical industries. At least 50 organizations in the US and the United Kingdom had data stolen.
The same report lists defense contractors, universities, law firms and political organizations among the targets.
The report says a Uyghur cultural site was apparently used to target members of that minority for surveillance.
Symantec says Budworm often focuses on government, technology and defense organizations. In August 2023 it hit a Middle Eastern telecommunications organization and an Asian government.
The BfV says APT27 has repeatedly attacked German companies since at least March 2021.
Dell SecureWorks said the group breached networks largely through watering-hole attacks launched from over 100 compromised legitimate websites.
The report says no zero-days were used. The group relied on old flaws such as CVE-2011-3544 and CVE-2010-0738, and used the PlugX remote access tool.
The BfV says the attacks exploited unpatched, internet-exposed servers, using flaws in Microsoft Exchange and Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus. The final payload was HyperBro.

A malware catalogue entry says HyperBro typically has three or more components, including a genuine loader and an encrypted, compressed payload. The entry lists report titles from other vendors and agencies that tie HyperBro to APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse, UNC215, BRONZE UNION and Emissary Panda.

In its 2023 report, Symantec saw Budworm load an updated SysUpdate backdoor by DLL sideloading. It also saw public tools such as AdFind, SecretsDump and PasswordDumper. Only credential harvesting was seen on the infected machines.
Kaspersky's GReAT team says several companies attribute the DRBControl backdoor, also known as Clambling, to APT27.
One analysis calls the Redosdru downloader commonly associated with APT27/Iron Tiger.
The MITRE record for the group lists tools including PlugX, HyperBro, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, China Chopper, Impacket, gh0st RAT and ZxShell.
An open-source test catalogue for disabling Windows event logging cites Threat Group 3390 (Bronze Union) as seen disabling HTTP logging on a Windows IIS web server.
Dell SecureWorks unveiled its report on the group at the Black Hat conference. The article was published on 5 August 2015.
The BfV warning on APT27 attacks against German companies was reported in January 2023. The agency published indicators of compromise and said it cannot rule out supply chain attacks.
Symantec reports that the two Budworm attacks with the updated SysUpdate variant both took place in August 2023.
In July 2025 Microsoft said it had observed two named Chinese nation-state actors, Linen Typhoon and Violet Typhoon, exploiting on-premises SharePoint server vulnerabilities.
Patch internet-facing servers promptly, and watch web servers for unexpected web shells and for changes to logging settings.
